title: Half the Dashboards Show 'No Data'
intro: After a Kubernetes upgrade last night, the team's service dashboards are blank. Nobody noticed until a customer reported slow checkouts — meaning you've been flying blind for hours.

steps.prompt: Check which scrape targets Prometheus considers down.
steps.hint: The 'up' metric exists for every target, even failing ones.

steps.prompt: Every checkout target is down. Get the scrape error details from the targets API.
steps.hint: lastError explains why each scrape failed.

steps.prompt: 404 on /metrics — the endpoint moved. Check what path the app actually serves metrics on now.
expected_commands: kubectl exec -it deploy/checkout -- curl -s localhost:8080/actuator/prometheus | head
steps.hint: Test from inside the pod to bypass any networking questions.

steps.prompt: After updating the scrape config's metrics_path to /actuator/prometheus, validate it before reloading.
steps.fake_output: SUCCESS: prometheus.yml is valid prometheus config file syntax

steps.hint: Targets should turn healthy within one scrape interval.

resolution: The app's framework upgrade (bundled into last night's release) moved its metrics endpoint from /metrics to /actuator/prometheus. Prometheus got 404s, marked every target down, and dashboards went blank — but no alert fired, because nobody had an alert on scrape targets being down. The fix was a one-line metrics_path change. The real lesson is monitoring your monitoring: an alert like 'up{job=~"..."} == 0 for 5m' (or absent(up{job="checkout-service"})) turns 'nobody noticed for hours' into a page within minutes. Missing data should itself be treated as an incident signal.
